The present appeal is filed by the appellants/
beneficiaries of the acquisition being aggrieved by the judgment and order dated 05.07.2018 passed
by the Iii- Additional District Judge, Kalaburagi in Laca No.52/2018 (hereinafter referred to as 'the
Appellate Court'), by which the Appellate Court while allowing the appeal with costs, had modified
the judgment and award dated 30.03.2015 in Lac No.144/2013 passed by the Senior Civil Judge,
Aland (hereinafter referred to as 'the Reference Court'), enhancing the compensation amount in
respect of the Nc: 2024:Khc-K:8160 acquired wet land from Rs.2,62,500/- per acre to
Rs.6,57,054/- per acre.

2.  The subject matter of the acquisition is the land in Sy.No.104/3, measuring 10 guntas, situated at Jawali- D, village of Aland Taluk, Kalaburagi District acquired for the purpose of Amarja Project in terms of the Notification dated 07.02.2009 issued under Section 4(1) of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894.
The SLAO had passed the award dated 15.02.2011 fixing the market value of the property at Rs.50,000/- per acre.
On a reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 the Reference Court enhanced the market value of the land to Rs.2,62,500/- per acre vide order dated 30.03.2015 in LAC No.144/2013.
On a further appeal for enhancement the Appellate Court by the impugned order dated 05.07.2018 passed in LACA No.52/2018 further enhanced the compensation amount to Rs.6,57,054/- per acre.

3. Though several grounds are urged in the memorandum of appeal, learned counsel for the appellants NC: 2024:KHC-K:8160 relying upon the judgment passed in MSA No.200103/2024,
dated 18.07.2024 in the case of Executive Engineer and Another VS. Laxman s/o Channabasappa and others submits that the present case is covered by the said order, in which this Court has The Chief Engineer And Anr vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61433312/
2 reduced the rate of compensation from Rs.6,57,054/- to Rs.6,43,507.5/- in view of the judgment passed in the case of Digamber s/o Ramrao, Kulkarni and Others VS.

sentences.text:
The Deputy Commissioner,
Kalaburagi and Others (in LACA Nos.347/2016 and 348/2016) wherein the acquisition was under the Notification dated 01.04.2010 for the similar purposes situated in the similar village.

He submits that since there was difference of one year between the Notification subject matter of case in Digamber and Notification subject matter of said appeal, 5% de-escalation was granted thereby reducing the compensation paid as above.

4. He submits Appellate Court instead of taking 5% de-escalation had taken only 3% de-escalation and NC: 2024:KHC-K:8160 that if compensation awarded by the Appellate Court is reduced by taking 5% de-escalation purpose of filing of the appeal would be served.
He further submits that the compensation awarded in MSA No.200103/2024 has already been paid and satisfied and same has attained finality.
5. Learned counsel for the respondent/claimant does not dispute the aforesaid factual aspect of the matter.

Since the order in MSA No.200103/2024 is passed in respect of the very same Notification dated 05.02.2009 in respect of the land which is situated in Jawali-D village, Aland Taluk,
Kalaburagi District, this Court do not see any reason to differ from the rate of compensation awarded in MSA No.200103/2024.
6.

Accordingly, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is partly allowed.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:8160 (ii) The compensation amount awarded by the Appellate Court in a sum of Rs.6,57,054/- per acre with all statutory benefit is reduced to Rs.6,43,507.5/- per acre.

(iii) It is made clear if there any delay by the claimants in filing the appeal before the Appellate Court, the said delayed period be excluded while calculating interest on the compensation.
Sd/-
(M.G.S.KAMAL) JUDGE SDU CT:PK The Chief Engineer And Anr vs The Special Land Acquisition Officer on 7 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61433312/
